brief: NDX closed below its 100-day moving average but stays inside the range since May, with the range's lower bound, the trendline and the 200-day average all still below current levels, and RSI nearing extremely oversold. SOX fell to a support area that has held since May and is at its most oversold since the Liberation Day selloff. Per GS, Info Tech had its largest percentage net selling since GS's 2016 records began, the most aggressively sold global sector this week, driven mainly by long liquidation plus short selling. A resilient market heading into Friday had attracted investors selling volatility for income, a trade that worked until it didn't. VIX then jumped to its highest level since July and VVIX surged 17 points, one of its largest moves in four years. Per GS, front-month VIX futures outperformed SPX sensitivity by 1.5 vol points, the widest gap since April, and asset managers entered the session with their largest net short VIX position on record, fueling the explosion. SPX is only modestly off its highs and roughly 250 points above its range lows, so the note reads the mismatch between the vol spike and equity move as forced deleveraging, not ordinary risk-off selling.
